why: The statement is a single universal yes/no question about multiplicity 1. The only post-snapshot event bearing on it directly is Shannon, Shiue, He and Saito (2025), which settles the conjecture for every k in four infinite families: a restriction of the question, so `case`; accepted by a journal of record (NNTDM, with received/revised/accepted dates) and approved by a named thesis committee, so `digested`. The close call is whether a restricted-family confirmation counts as a case rather than finitely many instances; it covers infinitely many k by proof, not a finite search, so `case`. Erdős #694, #416, #821, Lichtman, Li–Sha (F_2[x] analogue), Luca–Pollack and Ford's Sierpiński result answer different questions (max/min preimage ratio, totient counts, preimage growth, typical F(n), other multiplicities, polynomial rings) and are `variant`; the AI roles on #694/#416/#821 are recorded as `generated` from their own quotes but those events are discarded by scope. Finite-range checks are `instances`; Ford 1998's reformulation and density bound, Pomerance's sufficient condition and Erdős's 'infinitely many if any' bound or bear on nothing the statement quantifies, so `none`. Carmichael 1907 was retracted (`knocked_down`); the Saidak 'postcard' report is unsourced and ignored by all later literature (`not_credible`).
doubts: Shannon et al.: full text not read; novelty against earlier work (e.g. 2^t is classical) unchecked, and NNTDM is a modest venue, but nothing suggests an error. AI basis for #416/#821 is a repository-level statement, not the manuscripts' own disclosures; irrelevant here since those events are variants. Ford 1998's density bound liminf V₁/V ≤ 10^(−5·10^9) could arguably be read as a `bound`, but it is pre-snapshot and does not change any post-snapshot outcome.
